Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic) - next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token costs and unpredictable billing spikes with current OpenAI usage.
- Data governance concerns for Anthropic-hosted requests (sensitive PII flows).
- Latency variability for peak-hour customer-facing features.

Current stack and footprint:
- Production traffic: ~120 RPS for embeddings and 30 RPS for chat/generation (US region).
- Primary providers: OpenAI for chat + embeddings; Anthropic for a/B experiments.
- Most calls originate from our API gateway (k8s) and are proxied to provider endpoints.

Success criteria for migration off proprietary APIs (as discussed):
1) <=20% per-token cost reduction for embeddings workload at 95th percentile traffic.
2) Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for short chat prompts (<=256 tokens).
3) Compatibility: minimal engineering changes — ideally HTTP REST + OpenAI-compatible request/response shapes.
4) Data controls: ability to run in VPC/private deployment or ensure no customer prompt retention.

Model shortlist we talked through:
- RedPine-3B quantized (good cost/latency tradeoff for embeddings + chat)
- OpenLM-13B (higher quality for generative use-cases, needs GPU capacity)
- Claude-compatible alternative for Anthropic fallbacks (protocol compatibility)

Attachments: I’m including the security questionnaire draft and a sample migration plan template.

Proposed next steps:
- Action (Acme): share a redacted request sample for embeddings and a worst-case throughput window (John) — by EOD Friday.
- Action (Redwood): Rishi to prepare a cost estimate and latency projection for the shortlisted models (deliverable: approx numbers + suggested quantization) — ETA Tue 24 Mar.
- Action (joint): schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (network/security + sample requests) — propose Tue 24 or Wed 25.

If that looks right, I’ll get the calendar invite and attach the questionnaire officially.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

(555) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa — this is great and matches my notes. A few clarifications:

- For embeddings: typical batch is ~10k texts per hour; peak window last week was ~45k texts in a 10-minute burst during our nightly sync. I’ll redacted_sample_embeddings.zip to you by EOD.
- For compatibility: we need REST endpoints that accept OpenAI-like payloads (prompt, max_tokens, temperature, etc.) and return matching response fields so we don’t refactor our prompt orchestration layer heavily.
- For deployment: security wants an option for private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem) for critical PII flows — cloud-hosted with strict retention settings could work for non-PII features.

Agree on the shortlist; curious about whether you recommend starting with a hybrid approach (hosted for low-risk features, dedicated/private for PII).

I’m available Tue 24 after 11am PST for the technical deep-dive.
